arrival_intent: Follow a true story in which someone encounters a problem and something changes.
background: Enjoys essays with people, scenes and consequences; technical fluency is not the reason for reading.
desired_payoff: A turn that feels caused by what happened, rather than a lesson pasted onto the end.
drawn_in_by: A live situation, specific people and a change in what the author understood.
put_off_by: An incident that stops moving so the author can deliver a disguised checklist.
name: Story first reader
invariants: Tracks people, events, and consequences before abstract instruction.
Needs the account to preserve a credible connection between what happened and what changed.

variation_axes.description: How much adjacent subject knowledge the reader brings.

values.description: Little prior familiarity.
Recognizes neighboring ideas.
Has followed similar situations closely.

variation_axes.description: What most sustains attention in a story.

values.description: Concrete people and scenes.
Choices and consequences.
How experience changes understanding.

arrival_intent: Watch a person make a thing and discover why its final shape works.
background: Interested in process and decisions across writing, visual design, software or other crafts.
desired_payoff: The constraints, rejected routes and particular choice become visible in the finished object.
drawn_in_by: Material details, alternatives and the moment a better question changes the work.
put_off_by: A reveal of the final artefact that skips the thinking that made it possible.
name: Craft admirer
invariants: Looks for the choices and constraints that shaped the finished work.
Values process details when they explain why the result has its particular form.

variation_axes.description: How directly the reader practices a relevant craft.

values.description: Enjoys finished work without making similar things.
Has tried related creative or technical work.
Regularly makes work in a related craft.

variation_axes.description: Which part of making most interests the reader.

values.description: Limits and available materials.
Rejected approaches and trade-offs.
Iteration and the final shaping choices.

arrival_intent: Follow a film, comic, type or cultural reference into an unexpected subject.
background: Comfortable crossing subjects and interested in connections, not collecting references for their own sake.
desired_payoff: The reference changes how the main subject can be seen.
drawn_in_by: A vivid connection that survives beyond the opening joke or allusion.
put_off_by: A familiar name used as bait and then discarded without affecting the argument.
name: Cultural magpie
invariants: Enjoys connections across cultural forms and subject areas.
Needs a reference to change or illuminate the subject rather than serve as disposable bait.

variation_axes.description: How familiar the reader is with the reference material.

values.description: Knows little about the reference.
Recognizes it and knows a few details.
Follows the reference subject closely.

variation_axes.description: What kind of cross-subject connection most engages the reader.

values.description: A reference that makes an idea easier to picture.
A reference that changes how the subject is understood.
A connection that reveals a shared pattern.

arrival_intent: Understand why an unfamiliar practice or problem matters without becoming a specialist.
background: Intelligent reader with little prior knowledge of this article's technical or design domain.
desired_payoff: A clear mental picture and a reason to care that can be retold in ordinary language.
drawn_in_by: Concrete examples and terms introduced when their meaning becomes necessary.
put_off_by: Insider shorthand that makes entry impossible, or a remedial lecture that stalls the story.
name: Curious outsider
invariants: Wants to understand why the subject matters without becoming a specialist.
Needs unfamiliar terms and practices introduced when they become useful.

variation_axes.description: The reader’s starting familiarity with the poll subject.

values.description: Little prior knowledge of the subject.
Understands a neighboring field or practice.
Knows common terms but not specialist detail.

variation_axes.description: How the reader prefers unfamiliar ideas to be made clear.

values.description: Needs examples before abstractions.
Uses a careful analogy as a bridge.
Can follow terms once briefly defined.

arrival_intent: Find out how a decision affected the people who used, built or inherited the result.
background: May know the domain or not; follows consequences to people rather than systems alone.
desired_payoff: A credible account of who carried the burden and what became easier or harder.
drawn_in_by: Named responsibilities, specific friction and consequences that can be felt.
put_off_by: Architecture presented as self-justifying while the people living with it disappear.
name: Human stakes reader
invariants: Follows who carried the consequences of a decision.
Does not treat a system or architecture as self-justifying while affected people disappear.

variation_axes.description: How close the reader’s experience is to the consequences discussed.

values.description: No direct experience with similar consequences.
Has seen similar effects in a neighboring context.
Has personally navigated comparable consequences.

variation_axes.description: Which scale of consequence most draws attention.

values.description: Daily friction and immediate effects.
Accumulated effects over time.
How burdens and benefits are distributed.

arrival_intent: Recognise a fallible decision and learn how the author revised his understanding.
background: Has made consequential choices that looked reasonable at the time.
desired_payoff: An honest reconstruction of the mistaken belief, its cost and what changed afterward.
drawn_in_by: Self-implication and the awkward details that a victory story would omit.
put_off_by: Retrospective inevitability or an absent colleague made to carry all the blame.
name: Fellow mistake maker
invariants: Can recognize a reasonable decision that later proved mistaken.
Values candid reconstruction over retrospective inevitability or blame shifting.

variation_axes.description: How the reader relates to comparable mistakes.

values.description: Has faced a small number of such decisions.
Has repeated a plausible mistake across situations.
Has repaired a consequential past mistake.

variation_axes.description: What helps the reader understand responsibility.

values.description: The assumptions that seemed reasonable then.
How the decision affected other people.
The system and incentives around the decision.

arrival_intent: See whether new tools can help me make something worthwhile without needing permission from experts.
background: Builds or wants to build with AI, code or design tools without claiming formal mastery.
desired_payoff: A credible path to doing more while recognising where care and competence still matter.
drawn_in_by: Respect for imperfect beginnings and examples of growing judgment through making.
put_off_by: Gatekeeping, condescension or a demand to master every prerequisite before starting.
name: Hopeful maker
invariants: Wants to make something worthwhile without claiming mastery they do not have.
Welcomes practical possibility while recognizing the need for care and growing judgment.

variation_axes.description: How far the reader has progressed in making with relevant tools.

values.description: Has an idea but little hands-on experience.
Has made early attempts and learned from friction.
Regularly builds projects while still learning.

variation_axes.description: What kind of next step feels usable.

values.description: Wants a reversible first experiment.
Will try a bounded approach and inspect results.
Can pursue a larger step with explicit safeguards.

arrival_intent: Find an account of emerging technology that neither sells a miracle nor performs cynicism.
background: Has read too many confident claims about AI and wants proportion.
desired_payoff: A bounded claim supported by a real mechanism and its limits.
drawn_in_by: Specific evidence, costs and moments when the author changed his mind.
put_off_by: Grand forecasts, empty buzzwords or anti-hype posturing without an alternative.
name: Hype weary reader
invariants: Wants proportionate treatment of emerging technology.
Rejects both miracle claims and cynicism that offers no account of how something works.

variation_axes.description: How much repeated exposure the reader has had to confident technology claims.

values.description: Has seen a few broad claims.
Regularly encounters promotional narratives.
Is tired of repeated claims and familiar caveats.

variation_axes.description: What evidence most helps the reader assess a claim.

values.description: A clear account of how it works.
A fair comparison against alternatives.
Specific costs, failures, and boundary conditions.

arrival_intent: Take one usable move from this article into a problem I already have.
background: Has a live task and little need for a complete philosophy of the subject.
desired_payoff: A next step with enough conditions to know when to try it.
drawn_in_by: A concrete move, what it changed and the constraint that made it appropriate.
put_off_by: Insight that never becomes actionable, or a universal recipe detached from its case.
name: Practical borrower
invariants: Has a real problem and looks for a usable move.
Needs conditions that distinguish a suitable application from a universal recipe.

variation_axes.description: How soon the reader hopes to apply an idea.

values.description: Gathering ideas for a future task.
Working on a related task now.
Needs to make a near-term decision.

variation_axes.description: What form of practical takeaway best supports the reader.

values.description: A worked example to adapt.
A short sequence of checks.
A rule for choosing when to use an approach.

arrival_intent: Leave with a way to reason about similar decisions, not merely copy this solution.
background: Comfortable with complexity and interested in transferable distinctions.
desired_payoff: A decision rule that survives outside the author's exact circumstances.
drawn_in_by: Competing options, governing constraints and why one consideration outranked another.
put_off_by: A list of tactics with no principle connecting them, or an aphorism with no test.
name: Model builder
invariants: Looks for distinctions that transfer beyond the current example.
Wants competing options and constraints connected to a defensible principle.

variation_axes.description: How much experience the reader has modeling interacting systems.

values.description: Understands examples better than abstract system models.
Can reason about connected parts and their effects.
Regularly builds or evaluates formal models.

variation_axes.description: How far beyond the immediate case the reader seeks a reusable idea.

values.description: Wants to adapt the move to a similar case.
Wants a rule that generalizes across contexts.
Wants a model for reasoning about a class of decisions.

arrival_intent: Test where the apparent lesson stops being true.
background: Enjoys a strong argument enough to push it against difficult cases.
desired_payoff: A claim whose boundaries become sharper under pressure.
drawn_in_by: Visible assumptions, counterpressure and a concession that improves the argument.
put_off_by: A local success inflated into a rule for everyone.
name: Counterexample hunter
invariants: Tests where a promising claim stops being true.
Treats explicit limits as a way to sharpen an argument rather than weaken it.

variation_axes.description: The kind of pressure the reader first applies to a claim.

values.description: Looks for an exceptional case.
Tests the claim against common conditions.
Constructs a difficult opposing scenario.

variation_axes.description: What helps the reader decide whether a boundary is credible.

values.description: A causal explanation.
A contrast with a case where the claim fails.
A clear statement of where the claim does not apply.

arrival_intent: Ask what this choice leaves for the next person who must operate or change it.
background: Has inherited systems and knows the initial success is not the whole cost.
desired_payoff: A candid account of reversibility, handover and the burden after delivery.
drawn_in_by: Migration detail, operational consequences and documentation of why a path was chosen.
put_off_by: A clean ending at launch that transfers unresolved work to an invisible successor.
name: Maintainer inheritor
invariants: Looks beyond initial delivery to the person who must operate or change the result.
Values reversibility, clear reasoning, and honest treatment of unresolved work.

variation_axes.description: How directly the reader has inherited work from others.

values.description: Has occasionally taken over an unfamiliar project.
Frequently maintains work started by other people.
Owns systems where mistakes have costly downstream effects.

variation_axes.description: Which future maintenance concern most shapes the reader’s attention.

values.description: Keeping the current system running.
Adapting it as requirements evolve.
Making the reasoning legible to a successor.

arrival_intent: Decide whether forwarding this author's work for technical scrutiny would be worth the risk.
background: A weary hiring manager has reviewed many polished agentic-engineering portfolios; three promising links were dismissed by the architect.
desired_payoff: Enough legible, attributable evidence to make a confident forward-or-decline decision.
drawn_in_by: A short path from professional claim to inspectable decision, responsibility and consequence.
put_off_by: Another fluent pitch that makes the manager risk looking foolish when a technical peer opens the link.
name: Hiring evaluator
invariants: Assesses whether evidence supports the professional claims being made.
Considers the reputational cost of forwarding work that fails later scrutiny.

variation_axes.description: The reader’s role in deciding whether work advances.

values.description: Screens for relevance and clear evidence.
Decides whether a candidate merits team time.
Risks personal credibility when recommending the work.

variation_axes.description: How much inspectable detail the reader needs before making a recommendation.

values.description: Needs concrete evidence for each major claim.
Needs to inspect decisions and trade-offs.
Needs evidence likely to survive technical questioning.

arrival_intent: Strip the presentation away and test whether this author understands the engineering underneath.
background: A principal engineer or architect has already dismissed three similar forwarded portfolios and expects pattern vocabulary to conceal thin reasoning.
desired_payoff: A technical account that survives questions about mechanism, alternatives, cost, evidence and limits—or reveals where it does not.
drawn_in_by: Specific decisions and falsifiable detail that remain coherent under hostile scrutiny.
put_off_by: Named patterns, polished diagrams or confident outcomes that collapse when asked why this approach was chosen.
name: Jaded architect
invariants: Tests engineering claims beneath the presentation and pattern vocabulary.
Looks for mechanisms, alternatives, costs, evidence, and limits that withstand scrutiny.

variation_axes.description: Which engineering concern most shapes the reader’s scrutiny.

values.description: Boundaries, dependencies, and system structure.
Reliability, observability, and ongoing cost.
Implementation choices and evidence of execution.

variation_axes.description: How the reader approaches a claim that sounds polished.

values.description: Asks how the result was produced.
Asks what else was considered and why rejected.
Looks for evidence that could disprove the claim.

arrival_intent: Imagine solving a difficult problem alongside this author.
background: Could become a colleague or partner and cares about how disagreement and credit are handled.
desired_payoff: A sense that the author can reason openly, change course and make others effective.
drawn_in_by: Candid uncertainty, colleagues' contributions and decisions made with rather than over people.
put_off_by: Blame shifted onto absent teammates or a flawless-protagonist story.
name: Prospective collaborator
invariants: Imagines working through a difficult problem with the author.
Values open reasoning, fair credit, disagreement, and shared effectiveness.

variation_axes.description: The kind of working relationship the reader imagines.

values.description: A close day-to-day colleague.
A peer coordinating across teams.
A partner depending on delivered work.

variation_axes.description: What most helps the reader judge whether collaboration would work.

values.description: Evidence the author can change course.
Evidence others’ contributions are recognized.
Evidence conflict is handled constructively.
